summary: Go Read covers the core happy paths for text, range reads, notebooks, images, PDF attachments, ReadState, and several rich-result metadata probes, but it is not fully TS-exact. The highest-risk gaps are runtime and lifecycle differences: Go dedups reads from broader state than TS and stamps rich reads into state, PDF page selection/model/extraction behavior is a Go-only superset, cyber-risk reminder gating is not wired to the active model and can affect rich outputs, skill discovery and analytics/listeners fire at different times with different payloads, and the Go tool boundary lacks TS strict/output/permission metadata. Focused verification was run with `go test ./tools -run 'Test(FileReadTool|ReadFileState|CyberReminderGating|Alignment_FileRead)' -count=1` and currently fails at `TestFileReadToolRejectsOpenEndedPDFRangesOverLimit`, confirming one PDF selector parity gap.

gaps.title: Read does not expose the TS output/tool contract as a first-class Go contract
gaps.description: TS Read is a strict tool with an outputSchema discriminated by `type` (`text`, `image`, `notebook`, `pdf`, `parts`, `file_unchanged`) and tool metadata for max result size, read-only, concurrency, search/read classification, and auto-classifier input. Go has the public tool name and increasingly rich `ContentBlocks`/Metadata, but the shared tool interface is still Execute-only, the JSON schema cannot express strict-object rejection, and the TS result union is not the primary result contract. This leaves downstream consumers relying on string content plus metadata rather than the same structured shape TS returns.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares a strict input object and discriminated `outputSchema` for all Read variants.
TS sets maxResultSizeChars=Infinity, strict=true, concurrency-safe/read-only, auto-classifier, and search/read metadata.
The TS Tool interface carries input/output schemas, read-only/concurrency hooks, search/read classification, and maxResultSizeChars.

go_evidence.note: Go JSONSchema has no additionalProperties/strict-object field and ToolDefinition contains only name, description, and input_schema.
Go Tool exposes Name, Description, Schema, and Execute; ToolResult is string Content, ContentBlocks, NewMessages, and string Metadata.
Go has a FileReadResult helper and variant metadata, but production still stamps metadata onto ToolResult rather than returning the TS output union.
Read schema includes the public parameters but has no strict additionalProperties=false equivalent.

gaps.impact: Model-visible and programmatic consumers can observe different result structure, strictness, and lifecycle metadata from TS, even when the visible read content looks similar.

gaps.title: file_unchanged dedup applies to broader state and richer formats than TS
gaps.description: TS dedups only prior full Read-origin text/notebook state: it requires a non-partial entry whose `offset` is defined, and image/PDF branches never populate readFileState. Edit/Write/NotebookEdit deliberately write `offset: undefined` so the next Read cannot dedup against post-write state. Go checks only offset, limit, and mtime, ignores LastTool/source, stamps rich image/notebook/PDF reads into state, and uses a different file_unchanged stub. This can suppress content in Go where TS would re-read and can point the model at stale or unavailable prior rich content.

ts_evidence.note: TS dedup is killswitch-gated and requires existingState, not partial, and `existingState.offset !== undefined`; comments state images/PDFs are not cached.
Notebook reads set readFileState with offset and limit.
Image and PDF branches return without writing readFileState.
Text reads set readFileState with content, timestamp, offset, and limit.
TS file_unchanged stub is the long message telling the model to refer to the earlier Read tool_result.
TS Write refreshes readFileState with offset and limit undefined to prevent Read dedup against post-write state.
TS Edit also writes offset and limit undefined.

go_evidence.note: Go dedup compares Offset, Limit, and TimestampMs only; it does not check IsPartialView or LastTool/source.
Go stamps state for rich image/notebook/PDF reads and then can dedup them.
Go text reads set state with requestedOffset/requestedLimit and content, but without LastTool='Read'.
ReadFileEntry has Content and LastTool, so the data needed to restrict dedup by origin exists but is unused in Read dedup.
Go FileUnchangedStubText is `(no changes since last read)`, not the TS stub.
Go Write refreshes ReadState with LastTool='Write' but dedup does not inspect it.
Go Edit refreshes ReadState with LastTool='Edit' but dedup does not inspect it.
Go NotebookEdit refreshes ReadState with LastTool='NotebookEdit' but dedup does not inspect it.

gaps.impact: Go can return file_unchanged for reads TS would execute, especially after rich reads or writes/edits in the same timestamp window; model-visible stub text also differs.

gaps.title: Cyber-risk reminder gating is not wired like TS and can be appended to rich results
gaps.description: TS appends the cyber-risk reminder only in the text result mapper and uses the active main-loop model to skip exempt models. Go has a compatible constant and model exemption helper, but the active model is only set through a test/config setter and is not wired in SetupRegistry. When unset, Go falls back to path/content heuristics, so benign project files on non-exempt models may omit the TS reminder. Go also calls the append helper after rich reads, modifying ContentBlocks and Content for image/PDF/notebook summaries where TS does not append the reminder.

ts_evidence.note: TS appends CYBER_RISK_MITIGATION_REMINDER only in the `text` output mapping.
TS gates the reminder by getMainLoopModel canonical name and MITIGATION_EXEMPT_MODELS.

go_evidence.note: Go stores the active model in a package variable set by SetActiveModelForCyberGating; when non-empty and non-exempt it always appends.
When active model is empty, Go falls back to suspicious path/content heuristics instead of TS's non-exempt-model default.
SetupRegistry constructs FileReadTool without wiring active model or token/provider state into cyber gating.
Go calls maybeAppendCyberReminder after successful rich reads.
Go appends the reminder to both result.Content and result.ContentBlocks.
Tests preserve the Go fallback heuristic where normal project files do not get the reminder when active model is unset.

gaps.impact: Security guidance can be missing for ordinary text reads under default runtime wiring, and rich outputs can include an extra text block that TS never sends.

gaps.title: PDF page selection, model support, page-count fallback, and extraction lifecycle diverge
gaps.description: TS accepts a single page, bounded range, or open-ended range string syntactically, then rejects any open-ended range at validation time because it treats Infinity as over the 20-page cap. Go accepts comma-separated selectors, deduplicates pages, resolves open-ended selectors against real page count, and has tests for comma lists. TS page counting uses only `pdfinfo` and returns null on failure; Go falls back to Swift and raw byte scanning. TS rejects full PDF reads on unsupported Haiku 3 models and persists extracted page images under the tool results directory with an `outputDir` in the `parts` result. Go has no visible model support gate, uses temp extraction directories removed before returning, and returns only supplemental image NewMessages for pages.

ts_evidence.note: TS parsePDFPageRange supports only single page, `N-M`, and `N-`; no comma lists.
TS validates pages before I/O and treats an Infinity/open-ended range as over PDF_MAX_PAGES_PER_READ.
TS full-PDF support is gated by the current model, rejecting claude-3-haiku.
TS page count uses only pdfinfo and returns null if unavailable or unparsable.
TS `parts` result includes filePath, originalSize, count, and outputDir.
TS extraction writes images under getToolResultsDir()/pdf-uuid and returns that directory.
TS checks page threshold, computes shouldExtractPages, logs extraction analytics, and errors when full PDFs are unsupported by model.

go_evidence.note: Go parsePDFPageSelector accepts comma-separated lists, deduplicates pages, and models open-ended ranges.
Go invalid-pages message explicitly advertises comma-separated lists.
Go resolves open-ended page ranges against page count and filters comma-selected extracted images.
Go page count falls back from pdfinfo to Swift and then raw byte scanning.
Go extraction uses os.MkdirTemp and defers os.RemoveAll, so no persistent outputDir is available.
Go returns extracted page image blocks directly after reading temp files.
Go page reads return a text summary plus NewMessages image blocks, not a `parts` data object with outputDir.
Go full PDF path checks only page threshold and then inlines a document block; no isPDFSupported model gate appears.
Go tests lock in comma-separated page selector support.
A Go test expects `pages: "3-"` to be rejected, but the current implementation resolves the actual page count and the focused run fails this test.

gaps.impact: PDF reads can succeed, fail, paginate, emit attachments, or leave artifacts differently from TS; one focused Read test currently fails on this exact selector behavior.

gaps.title: Read path permission/observer lifecycle is approximated inside Execute
gaps.description: TS Read participates in the central permission and observable-input lifecycle before the tool call: it expands observable paths, exposes getPath, prepares wildcard permission matchers, checks explicit read-deny rules without I/O, and bypasses UNC I/O before permission. Go enforces allowed directories and verifies the opened file descriptor, which is strong local safety, but the shared Tool interface has no Read-specific permission hooks or observable-input backfill. Generic parsing also ignores unknown keys, so TS strict-object rejection is not enforced at runtime.

ts_evidence.note: TS Read defines getPath, backfillObservableInput, preparePermissionMatcher, and checkPermissions.
TS validateInput expands paths, checks deny rules before I/O, bypasses UNC probing, rejects binary extensions, and blocks special devices.
TS expandPath trims, expands ~, handles relative paths against getCwd, converts Windows POSIX paths, and normalizes NFC.

go_evidence.note: Go Tool has no getPath/backfill/permission matcher/checkPermissions hook.
parseInput uses json.Unmarshal into structs, which silently ignores unknown object keys.
Go checkAllowedPath enforces allowed directories by resolving symlinks, but only as tool-internal Execute logic.
Go performs allowed-dir, device, binary-extension, open, and fd verification inside Execute.
UpdateSessionContext wires allowed dirs into FileReadTool but does not expose TS-style observer/permission hooks.

gaps.impact: Policy, UI, audit, and strict-schema consumers cannot observe or decide on Read exactly where TS does, and unknown model inputs can be accepted in Go.

gaps.title: File reading limits and token counting do not follow TS precedence or exact counter path
gaps.description: TS computes default file-reading limits from env var, GrowthBook override, and hardcoded defaults, then lets ToolUseContext override maxSizeBytes/maxTokens and logs override analytics. Token validation estimates first and then calls the API tokenizer near the limit. Go uses constants for text size/token limits, has an optional TokenBudgetProvider only for rich image/PDF budgets, and SetupRegistry does not wire that provider. Text token checks use a Go tiktoken estimate path rather than TS API counting, so boundary behavior and operational controls can differ.

ts_evidence.note: TS limit precedence is env max tokens, GrowthBook override, then defaults, with includeMaxSizeInPrompt and targetedRangeNudge flags.
TS applies ToolUseContext fileReadingLimits and logs tengu_file_read_limits_override when overrides are supplied.
TS validates tokens using roughTokenCountEstimationForFileType and countTokensWithAPI before throwing MaxFileReadTokenExceededError.

go_evidence.note: Go hardcodes defaultReadMaxSizeBytes and defaultReadMaxTokens as constants.
FileReadTool has an optional TokenBudgetProvider for remaining model tokens.
Go falls back to defaultReadTokenBudget when TokenBudgetProvider is nil.
SetupRegistry constructs FileReadTool without TokenBudgetProvider or fileReadingLimits wiring.
Go text reads use defaultReadMaxSizeBytes and tieredEstimateReadTokens with defaultReadMaxTokens.
Go token validation uses local fast/precise estimation rather than TS countTokensWithAPI.

gaps.impact: Operators cannot tune Read behavior through the same controls, prompts may show different guidance, and files near token/byte limits may be accepted or rejected differently.

gaps.title: Skill discovery timing and conditional activation do not match TS session lifecycle
gaps.description: TS discovers nearby skill directories and activates conditional skills after dedup but before the file read, skips the whole flow in CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE, records dynamicSkillDirTriggers for attachment display, and starts directory loading asynchronously. Go invokes discovery only after a successful read, has no visible simple-mode guard in FileReadTool, ignores per-name trigger matches, and the skills Manager conditional activation hook is effectively a cache-warming no-op. This changes which reads can surface skills and when they become active or visible.

ts_evidence.note: TS skips simple mode, discovers skill dirs before callInner, records dynamicSkillDirTriggers, asynchronously adds directories, and activates conditional skills for paths.

go_evidence.note: Go wires FileReadTool.SkillManager to the shared SkillTool manager.
Go invokes analytics/listeners/skill activation only in afterSuccessfulRead after content was read.
Go discovers nearby skill dirs with its own upward walk and repo-root heuristics.
Go can look up dynamic skills for a path, but FileReadTool currently discards the returned names.
Go ActivateConditionalForPath is documented as a no-op/cache warm hook for future parity.
Other Go surfaces explicitly check CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE, but FileReadTool's skill activation path does not show that guard.

gaps.impact: Skills can be missing when TS would attach/activate them, or loaded in simple mode/after success where TS would not; conditional activation semantics are not equivalent.

gaps.title: Read analytics and listener scope/signatures differ from TS
gaps.description: TS fileReadListeners receive `(filePath, content)` and are called only on the text read path after the content is available. TS session analytics includes total/read lines, total/read bytes, offset, optional limit, extension, optional messageID, and session-memory/session-transcript booleans. Go invokes basic and rich listeners for every successful read variant with mtime/partial/byte/line metadata but no content, emits a simplified `tengu_session_file_read`, and emits a second kind-based event for session files. The gap is not just field names; it changes listener side effects and analytics cardinality.

ts_evidence.note: TS fileReadListener signature is `(filePath, content)`.
TS invokes listeners only on the text path, with resolvedFilePath and content.
TS `tengu_session_file_read` payload includes totalLines, readLines, totalBytes, readBytes, offset, optional limit/ext/messageID, and session booleans.

go_evidence.note: Go basic listener receives absPath, mtimeMs, and isPartialView; rich listener receives metadata, not file content.
Go afterSuccessfulRead emits simplified analytics and invokes both listener sets for every successful read variant.
The same afterSuccessfulRead also triggers skill activation, tying listener timing to all variants.
Go alignment tests currently assert a lineCount/ext-oriented analytics shape rather than the richer TS payload.
Go integration tests lock in listener arguments as path plus mtime, not path plus content.

gaps.impact: Services depending on text content listeners, TS analytics fields, or per-read event counts will behave differently in Go.

gaps.title: Path expansion and per-session cwd normalization are not TS-equivalent for base Read
gaps.description: TS expandPath trims input, expands `~`, resolves relative paths against async-local getCwd, converts Windows POSIX-style paths, and normalizes NFC before validation, permission checks, and state keys. Go base Read trims file_path and uses filepath.Abs/Clean around the process cwd and ReadState key normalization. Agent-specific wrappers rewrite relative paths for subagents, but base FileReadTool is not injected with RuntimeScope/current cwd, so session cwd, home expansion, NFC, and Windows path conversion semantics are not the same at the core tool boundary.

ts_evidence.note: TS expandPath handles trim, empty path, ~ expansion, absolute/relative resolution, Windows POSIX path conversion, and NFC normalization.
TS getCwd uses AsyncLocalStorage override for concurrent agents and falls back to original cwd.
TS backfills observable file_path with expandPath before observers see it.
TS call uses expandPath for fullFilePath normalization.

go_evidence.note: Go trims file_path and normalizes macOS screenshot spaces but does not perform full TS expandPath semantics.
Go normalizes with filepath.Clean and filepath.Abs against the process cwd.
ReadFileState is keyed on filepath.Abs-normalized paths.
Go subagent wrapper rewrites relative file_path/path inputs against an agent base cwd.
Agent sessions wrap the registry for cwd, but base FileReadTool has no RuntimeScope cwd field.
SetupRegistry creates RuntimeScope but constructs FileReadTool only with AllowedDirs and ReadState.

gaps.impact: Relative paths, `~`, Unicode normalization, and concurrent-session cwd behavior can resolve differently from TS, and observer/permission state sees a different path lifecycle.

gaps.title: Read parity tests include stale comments, Go-only expectations, and one currently failing selector test
gaps.description: The Go test suite has useful coverage but does not yet form a clean TS parity baseline. Some alignment-test comments still say every case should fail even though the implementation now has FileReadResult and variant metadata. Other tests explicitly lock Go-only behavior such as comma-separated PDF page selectors. A focused Read test command currently fails on open-ended PDF range handling, which is a real parity mismatch against TS validation.

ts_evidence.note: TS outputSchema variants are the authoritative structured result baseline.
TS page selector grammar is single page/range/open range only.
TS open-ended ranges are rejected by the max-pages validation before I/O.

go_evidence.note: Header says tests are intentionally RED and fail today, which is stale for implemented surfaces such as FileReadResult/variant metadata.
Tests expect FileReadResult and text variant metadata; those surfaces now exist in Go.
Tests lock in comma-separated PDF selector support, a Go-only grammar relative to TS.
The open-ended PDF range test expects TS-like rejection but currently fails because the implementation accepts the resolved range.
Implementation resolves open-ended page ranges using actual page count, explaining the current focused test failure.

gaps.impact: Future implementers can chase stale failures or preserve Go extensions unintentionally; verification cannot distinguish deliberate TS parity from local enhancements.
